work_packages.name: A change that adds a string error, a hidden reach across packages, an environment read in a library or a copied device request is refused by `./dev check`
work_packages.quality_bar: As strict and as plain as Clippy under `-D warnings` and rust-lang's own `tidy`: the smallest real violation fails, the message names the file, the rule and what to write instead, and code that was already there is left alone.

items.statement: Each rule the design's table marks WP1 refuses its violation and passes the corrected code: for every such rule a fixture with one violation fails with the rule's name, the file and the line, and the same fixture corrected passes. `library-env` passes a read in a package registered `test_role = "support"` and refuses the same read in an engine library. `history-names` refuses a code in a file name, an environment variable name, a Cargo target name and a Cargo description.
items.ask: Read the test and the rules. Does every rule marked WP1 have a violating and a corrected fixture? Do the fixtures include a `pub fn` whose `Result<_, String>` return spans two lines, an `include_str!` that climbs out of its package with `..`, a dependency from a package under `crates/` on one under `examples/`, and `THRUM_G5_CAPTURE_DIR` read in a file whose own name is clean? Is a name such as `rgba8` or `vec3` left alone?

items.statement: A registered rule's total can only go down. In a scratch Git repository, a change that adds a violation is refused; a change that adds a violation and rewrites the baseline to match is refused before it is committed, after it is committed, and from a second worktree of the same repository; and removing a violation lowers the mark that later changes are held to. A file moved or split with its violations, a newly registered rule and a new version of a rule pass. A rule built on a branch whose base then gains a violation is refused while the branch's history still holds the lower count, and passes once the branch first lists the rule in a commit that holds the new base's counts.
items.ask: Read the ratchet cases. Is the accepted total taken from the baseline's Git history and never from the working tree's baseline? Does the committed case run the check at the commit that raised the count, with no remote and no branch name given? After a violation that reached history is removed, does the check pass again with nothing waived? In the moved-base case, is the passing branch one whose every commit holds a baseline equal to its own tree?

items.statement: At the claimed commit the whole repository passes every rule against a checked-in baseline that holds each file's present count and nothing else, and `--zero` on a path fails wherever a violation of the named rule exists under it, and for a path that does not exist.
items.ask: Run `check --rule string-errors --zero crates/thrum-app` and `check --rule package-reach --zero crates/thrum-render`: does each fail and list the sites the review named there? Does the baseline hold any count above what its file has now?

items.statement: `./dev check` and `./dev check-docs` run the rules through `repo_check.py`, with no flag, feature or environment variable that skips them. A refusal names the patterns section to read and the shape to use, and the patterns reference names the rule that holds each shape.
items.ask: Could a builder who has never seen the review fix a refusal of each rule from its message alone? Does any path through `./dev check` skip the rules?

items.statement: The counts the rules found are on record for each rule marked WP1, in each crate and example, at the commit the build started from. Every difference between that record and the baseline at the claimed commit names the commit on the main branch that made it.
items.ask: Does the record give a count for every rule and package, taken from the rules' own output at a named commit? Where a total differs from what the review reported for string errors, reaches across packages or environment reads, does the record say why? Is every violation the baseline holds beyond the starting record the work of a commit that reached the main branch before the rules did, and none of them this work package's own?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this work package moved no retained image.

work_packages.name: The checkout no longer carries bulk media: every file that left is listed, comes back by one command, and every link still resolves
work_packages.quality_bar: Nothing a reader could open before is lost, as with a careful `git lfs migrate`, but with no new service: the tree is lighter, each removed file is one command away with a hash that proves it, and no document was rewritten to hide a hole.

items.statement: No tracked file under `docs/evidence/` is over 2 MiB except the registered exact-baseline references. Every history entry in the manifest matches its blob in the object store, every local entry the store holds matches its hash, and a new `evidence-size` rule, with its fixtures, refuses a new oversized file.

Every file that left the tree is a history entry in `docs/evidence/BULK.json` with its path, size, SHA-256, Git blob and the last commit that held it, and `restore` writes back bytes with that SHA-256. `put` stores a new file in the one local store beside the main checkout and lists it as a local entry, with no blob or commit; a file put from one worktree is restored with the same hash in another worktree of the repository.
items.ask: Read the test. From a clean checkout, does it restore the largest file, a video and a sample of others, and compare hashes it computes itself? Does it make two worktrees of a scratch repository, put a file from one and restore it in the other? Does `restore` fail loudly for a path that is in neither history nor the local store, and does `check` name a local entry whose file is not on this machine without failing?

items.statement: Every link in tracked Markdown still resolves, to a tracked file or to a path the manifest lists, whether or not a restored copy is on disk, and no review, record or `DESIGN.md` was edited to make it so. A link to a path that is neither tracked nor listed is still refused.
items.ask: Does the work package's diff change any file under `docs/plans/`, or the text of any review or record under `docs/evidence/`? Pick three links from reviews to files that left: does each resolve through the manifest, and does `restore` bring the file back?

items.statement: A builder with a new large capture knows what to do from the refusal and the storage rules: keep it in scratch with the record that reproduces it, or `put` it in the local store. `docs/ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` say so.
items.ask: From the `evidence-size` refusal and the two documents alone, what does a builder do with a 60 MB real-time capture that a reviewer must see? Is any step missing, and is anything said about a remote copy that does not exist?

items.statement: The tracked tree's size before and after is on record, with the count and bytes that left by file type, and what a cap of 1 MiB and of 0.5 MiB would remove.
items.ask: Are the figures taken from `git ls-files` at named commits? How large is `docs/evidence` in a fresh checkout after this work package?

work_packages.name: The repository gate passes with migrated plans
work_packages.quality_bar: The merge gate passes with the existing rule versions and ratchet, and legacy evidence is recoverable from a full clone.

items.statement: The shape-rule suite guards the production reader in `./dev check` by verifying that it finds a known item check in a checked-in `DONE.json`. With `work_packages` fixtures, `script-caller` recognizes a script named only by an item check in both an open and a Done work package and refuses it when unnamed. `test-binary` recognizes named targets, and history-name pins expire when their work package is Done.

The repository guard passes on the migrated plans with the existing rule versions and baseline. Its link check accepts a tracked page's link to the manifest-listed G7 record's `#checks` heading both before and after byte-for-byte restore. With G7 restored, a missing-file link added to the tracked page is still reported.

Git tracks no files under `docs/evidence/`. The three legacy records listed in the WP5 plan are history entries in the live manifest and recover byte for byte from the blobs at their original paths in `77c70eaac`.
items.check: PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 -c 'from evidence_store import ROOT, content, entries, git, tracked; paths = ("docs/evidence/CULLING/M2.md", "docs/evidence/render/cooked-draw/BASE", "docs/evidence/v1-workload/G7-CHROME-VALLEY-2026-11-07.md"); manifest = {entry["path"]: entry for entry in entries(ROOT)}; assert not any(path.startswith("docs/evidence/") for path in tracked(ROOT)); assert all(manifest[path]["kind"] == "history" and content(ROOT, manifest[path]) == git(ROOT, "show", "77c70eaac:" + path) for path in paths)'

items.statement: The shared exact-images run covers the WP5 landing with every registered Mac and Chrome baseline passing.

items.statement: The top level of `scripts/` holds only what `./dev`, an open item's check or the baseline registry names. Every other script is in a named subfolder, and an index says in one line what each folder is for.

Each document under `docs/design/` that a module design in `docs/plans/` supersedes says so in its first lines and links to what replaced it, and one index lists which documents are current authority. No path under `docs/design/` changed.
